THE ALASKA AI DOCKET, as published on 2026-10-31.

This is the complete public record behind alaskaaihq.com. It is two things: a docket of tracked Alaska decisions about artificial intelligence, and the Cook Inlet Gas Watch, a daily numeric record of Southcentral Alaska's natural gas position.

Cite a docket item by writing its id in double brackets, like [[enstar-cook-inlet-gas-storage]]. The page turns that into a link.

  2026-08-21  Glenfarne answered, and the answer is a schedule. Neither chamber met on the bill. --- enstar-cook-inlet-gas-storage ---
Title: Enstar's Cook Inlet gas storage plan (Kenai Loop Pool)
Kind: regulatory-docket | Status: open-for-comment | Decider: Regulatory Commission of Alaska (prudency); Alaska DNR (storage lease and technical determination) | Location: Kenai Loop Pool, Cook Inlet near Kenai
Public access: open. Anyone may comment on the Division of Oil and Gas's preliminary written finding for the Kenai Loop storage lease until 5 p.m. on November 13th, per the state's public notice. The RCA prudency question stays with the commission, a governor-appointed, legislature-confirmed body whose dockets the public reaches through formal comment and intervention.
First seen 2026-07-11. Last updated 2026-10-28.
Summary: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska denied Enstar's request for an advance determination that its proposed Cook Inlet gas storage project was prudent, in a 17-page order the Anchorage Daily News reported on July 10th, saying the utility lacked basic information. The $240 million plan would have bought the depleted Kenai Loop Pool from AIX Energy to hold 25 billion cubic feet of gas, close to half Enstar's annual demand, and Enstar suspended it after the order. The commission denied Enstar's petition for reconsideration 3 to 2 on August 21st, with a written order to follow. Enstar applied to the Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission on September 17th to store gas in the Kenai Loop field, with a hearing tentatively set for November 12th. On October 13th the Division of Oil and Gas issued a preliminary written finding that a Kenai Loop storage lease to ENSTAR would best serve the state's interest, ahead of Hilcorp's competing application, and public comment on that finding runs until 5 p.m. on November 13th.

Donna Mears in January 2026, would have set utility rate-setting guidelines and community benefit agreement standards for large energy use facilities such as data centers, and given the Regulatory Commission of Alaska new duties over them.
